whatWasLearnedThatIsWorthMoreThanThePart.THE_SEARCH_TRAP: Three of the six unresolved cities are blocked not by obscurity but by a WRONG NAMESAKE that a keyword search returns with high confidence: 'Mart, TX' returns Martindale, TX; 'Crawford, TX' returns Crawford, NEBRASKA (the retrieved ordinance's own text cites Nebraska law); 'Creedmoor, TX' returns Creedmoor, NORTH CAROLINA (districts named after NC highways). Two of the three are out-of-state, and both wrong sites look official. Any agent doing the remaining 19 cities will hit this same trap, and the failure is silent: the imported district list is internally consistent and reads as authoritative. The admissibility rule that catches it is recorded in the classification artifact.
whatWasLearnedThatIsWorthMoreThanThePart.THE_TABLE_CANNOT_BE_SEARCH_SUMMARY_DERIV: Related and independently sufficient: setback cell writes are sticky for everything but `unaccounted`, so a class is not a hypothesis this lane may hold loosely. That combination -- silent wrong-city sources plus irreversible writes -- is why the classification's evidence grade is recorded per row rather than as a single confidence.

P-326 named this defect and left it; it is still unowned. P-300's design must read the zoning rail (or a table that encodes the answer) on that branch, and any successor should know that the defect and P-300's fix are the same edit.

THE STICKY-WRITE ASYMMETRY, which is the reason for this lane's caution and the most reusable thing found: because setbackCellMayBeMoved releases `unaccounted` and this job's own false absences but not `refused` or a true `absent-verified`, the FIRST correct classification a parcel receives is the one it keeps. A lane that writes classes without a source read is not making a reversible approximation; it is making a permanent one.

fleetMemory.LESSON: A keyword search for a US city's zoning code can return a DIFFERENT CITY, and for two of the forty here the different city was in a different STATE with that state's law in its own text. The wrong result is internally consistent, comes from a plausible-looking official domain, and carries no internal signal that it is wrong. Admit a source only if it names the city AND the correct county, or is the city's own site with a Texas address in it.

When a write path releases only its weakest state for correction and freezes every stronger one, the classification feeding that write is not a working hypothesis. Establish the source read BEFORE the code path exists, or the code path will be the thing that makes the guess permanent.
